Package com.stockly.service

Class InventoryManager

java.lang.Object
com.stockly.service.InventoryManager
public class InventoryManager extends Object
The heart of the application: all inventory business logic lives here and nowhere else.

Responsibilities:

  • Add, update, delete and look up products (CRUD).
  • Validate every input and report problems with clear messages.
  • Keep an ObservableList of products so that the TableView, dashboard cards and report automatically refresh when data changes.
  • Calculate statistics (totals, counts per StockStatus).
  • Record a recent-activity feed.
  • Save to the InventoryRepository after every change; if saving fails, the change is rolled back so memory and disk never disagree.

This class contains no user-interface code (no dialogs, no controls), only JavaFX collections.

Author:
Umama Wahab

  • Method Details

    • load

      public void load() throws PersistenceException
      Replaces the in-memory inventory with the data stored in the repository. Used at start-up and by the "Refresh" button. If reading fails, the current data is left untouched.
      Throws:
      PersistenceException - if the stored data cannot be read

    • addProduct

      public Product addProduct(String name, int quantity) throws InventoryException
      Adds a new product. The name is trimmed, the stock status is assigned automatically and the inventory is saved.
      Parameters:
      name - the product name (see validateName(String))
      quantity - the initial number of units (0 to 1000000)
      Returns:
      the newly created product, including its generated id
      Throws:
      ValidationException - if the name or quantity is invalid, or another product already has this name
      PersistenceException - if the inventory cannot be saved (the addition is rolled back)
      InventoryException

    • updateProduct

      public boolean updateProduct(int id, String name, int quantity) throws InventoryException
      Updates the name and quantity of an existing product.
      Parameters:
      id - the id of the product to update
      name - the new name
      quantity - the new quantity
      Returns:
      true if something changed, false if the new values equal the old ones
      Throws:
      ProductNotFoundException - if no product has this id
      ValidationException - if the name or quantity is invalid, or another product already has this name
      PersistenceException - if the inventory cannot be saved (the change is rolled back)
      InventoryException

    • getProducts

      public javafx.collections.ObservableList<Product> getProducts()
      Returns the live list of all products. The list cannot be modified directly - use addProduct(java.lang.String, int), updateProduct(int, java.lang.String, int) and deleteProduct(int) - but it can be observed, which is how the user interface stays up to date.
      Returns:
      an unmodifiable observable list of products

      public static boolean matches(Product product, String query, StockStatus status)

      public static String validateName(String name) throws ValidationException

    • parseQuantity

      public static int parseQuantity(String text) throws ValidationException
      Converts the text typed into the quantity field into a number, rejecting invalid input. Accepted: whole numbers from 0 to 1000000. Rejected: empty text, letters, decimals, negative numbers and values that are too large.
      Parameters:
      text - the raw text typed by the user
      Returns:
      the quantity as an int
      Throws:
      ValidationException - with a message that explains exactly why the text was rejected

    • validateQuantity

      public static void validateQuantity(int quantity) throws ValidationException
      Validates a quantity that is already a number.
      Parameters:
      quantity - the quantity to check
      Throws:
      ValidationException - if it is negative or above 1000000
